subject: question about prediction on zero inflated negative distributions using inla.posterior.sample()

messages.author: 929e733ff7821ad3
messages.subject: question about prediction on zero inflated negative distributions using inla.posterior.sample()
parts:
hi all,

I am trying to make predictions on a zero inflated negative distribution (zeroinflatednbinomial1 in this case) from a model with fixed effect and spatial random effects.

I used inla.posterior.sample() function to get the simulated posterior distribution of the model output:

sim   <- inla.posterior.sample(n=N_sim, result=myfit)

I am wondering how the simulated false zero probability is incoperated in the output sim.  For the ith simulated sample, is the false zero p simulated as 
sim[[i]]$hyperpar[2]? or is it already included in the simulated spatial random effect part w?

let beta=sim[[i]$latent[index_for_fixed_effect] be the simulated fixed effects coefficients,  w=sim[[i]$latent[index_for_spatial_random_effects] ) be the simulated spatial random effect, so the simulated ZINB distribution has the following parameters: mu=beta+w (if only intercept as the fixed effect), falsezero_pi=sim[[i]]$hyperpar[2], size=sim[[i]]$hyperpar[1] ? is this correct?

Thanks

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] question about prediction on zero inflated negative distributions using inla.posterior.sample()
parts:
Dear Lisa,

All fixed (beta) and random effects (w) only contribute to the negative binomial part. The zero inflation is only handled by its hyperparameter. So you are correct, assuming that you used the correct indices for hyperpar.

Best regards,
